summary: A seasonal guide to local hiking trails as places for adventure and photography, running from autumn into early winter. It profiles hikers and photographers on specific named trails and dates, from Maple Whisper Trail foliage to Milky Way astrophotography. It also stresses a leave-no-trace respect for wildlife and the changing beauty of the trails.
one_line: A narrative guide to local hiking trails showing seasonal beauty and photography spots from October to December 2023, with named hikers and trails.
key_facts: Since September 1, 2023, the local trails have been alive with hikers and photographers.
On October 21st, Claire Thompson, a local nature photographer, captured "the symphony of colors" on the Maple Whisper Trail, known for vibrant reds and golds.
A group led by veteran trail-guide Marcus Lee reached the summit of Eagle's Crest the following weekend, with views of the Snake River below.
On November 5th, amateur wildlife photographer Emily Watson photographed an elusive Red-Tailed Hawk in flight on the Whispering Pines Path.
Hikers are reminded to leave no trace and respect wildlife.
On November 12th, Paul Richardson's pre-dawn hike captured morning mist, shadow, and dewdrops.
Winter rains in late November create new streams near Cerulean Cascade Trail, whose falls attract photographers like Lisa Kim.
In December, Jacob Mills explored the less-crowded Willow Wisp Trail, finding frost patterns on a fallen log.
On December 20th, the Harris family hiked the Evergreen Loop, a trail suited to all ages.
Trekker Oliver Saunders was photographed in silhouette at sunset by his partner Hazel on December 27th.
Astrophotographer Rajiv Chen photographed the Milky Way from the trail on December 30th.
